## TIER 2 — per-component gap detail (core + common; edge summarized)

### AlertDialog — 21 gaps (0 core) · gaps-core
_Port-code needed:_ Two genuinely missing PORT behaviors require new implementation, both CORE: (1) Action/Cancel buttons must actually CLOSE the dialog on click — today they are inert PlainHTML inside the content array with no close wiring, so the only close path is Escape/SetOpen; an alert dialog whose Cancel/Action buttons do nothing is fundamentally broken. (2) onOpenAutoFocus must focus the CANCEL button specifically (the defining alertdialog a11y override, alert-dialog.tsx:126-129), not the generic first-tabbable that captureFocus uses — currently coincidental because Cancel is the first tabbable in the golden story. Both need either a compound API or dedicated `action`/`cancel` Input slots with close handlers and a cancel focus marker. Secondary: defaultOpen does not run the portal/envelope path (overlay renders un-portaled, no scroll-lock/focus-guards/cancel-focus) because that work lives only in openDialog, not in Initialize.
_Coverage today:_ Six committed oracles cover this component. DOM: golden-dom/alertdialog.open.txt and alertdialog.closing.txt (full body-portaled tree: data-scroll-locked body, two data-radix-focus-guard spans, aria-hidden #root, the rt-AlertDialogOverlay/Scroll/ScrollPadding/Content anatomy, role=alertdialog, aria-labelledby/aria-describedby links, data-state=open/closed, --max-width normalized to <px>, ids→<idN>). ARIA: golden-aria/alertdialog.rest.txt (button only), alertdialog.open.txt (alertdialog "Revoke access" tree with heading/paragraph/2 buttons), plus .axe.txt fingerprints (color-contrast only) at rest+open. Drivers in themes-states.mjs: STATES.alertdialog.open (click trigger, wait role=alertdialog) and CLOSE.alertdialog=escClose, so the closing-DOM oracle exercises the Escape close path. themes-a11y.mjs auto-runs rest+open via the shared MATRIX. NOT COVERED: there is ZERO APG keyboard entry for alertdialog in themes-apg.mjs (only `dialog` has APG checks) — so focus-into-dialog-on-open, Tab-trap, and Escape-closes-restores-focus are unverified for alertdialog; the DEFINING alertdialog contracts (focus the CANCEL button specifically on open; outside-click does NOT close) are verified nowhere; no controlled-mode, defaultOpen, closeOnEscape=false, empty-title/description, or focus-restore oracle exists.
- [core/missing-in-port/a11y] **onOpenAutoFocus focuses the CANCEL button on open (cancelRef.current.focus), NOT the first tabbable. This is the single defining a11y difference of AlertDialog vs Dialog: the user must land on the safe/non-destructive action.**
  - alert-dialog.tsx:126-129 (onOpenAutoFocus → cancelRef.current?.focus({preventScroll:true})); cancelRef set via AlertDialogContent context + AlertDialogCancel useComposedRefs (lines 117,215-218); asserted by alert-dialog.test.tsx:60-62 'should focus the cancel button' → PORT FIX: the port calls the generic captureFocus (FocusScope.purs:65, focuses first tabbable) in AfterOpen — it does NOT focus a designated cancel element. In the current golden the Cancel button happens to be the first tabbable so it coincides, but reorder Cancel after Action and the port breaks. Add a `cancelTarget`/cancel-button marker to Input and focus it explicitly. ORACLE: add an APG check id:alertdialog name:'open focuses the Cancel button' — after open, assert document.activeElement is the Cancel button (e.g. activeIs of the soft/gray button), deterministic.
- [core/in-port-but-unverified/pointer] **Outside-click (pointer-down-outside / interact-outside) NEVER closes the dialog — both handlers are unconditionally preventDefault'd. An alert dialog can ONLY be dismissed by an explicit Action/Cancel/Escape.**
  - alert-dialog.tsx:130-131 (onPointerDownOutside={e=>e.preventDefault()}, onInteractOutside={e=>e.preventDefault()}); the Content type Omits onPointerDownOutside/onInteractOutside (lines 106-109) → Port correctly renders NO overlay onClick handler (AlertDialog.purs overlayContent has no HE.onClick, unlike Dialog.purs:277). But nothing verifies it. ORACLE: APG/runtime check id:alertdialog — open, then pg.mouse.click on the overlay backdrop outside the content (or click rt-AlertDialogScroll padding), assert role=alertdialog still visible. Deterministic.
- [core/in-port-but-unverified/keyboard] **Escape closes and restores focus to the trigger (default closeOnEscape).**

ORACLE: clone the three dialog APG checks (themes-apg.mjs:76-80) for id:alertdialog — 'Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger' (assert activeIs('#root button')). Deterministic.

- [core/in-port-but-unverified/a11y] **open moves focus INTO the dialog on open (focus leaves the trigger).**

### NavigationMenu — 28 gaps (4 core) · gaps-core
_Port-code needed:_ Genuinely missing PORT-CODE (needs new implementation, not just an oracle): (1) the full open/close TIMER state machine — delayDuration (default 200) delayed-open, skipDelayDuration (default 300) skip-delay window with isOpenDelayed, the 150ms startCloseTimer on trigger/content leave, onContentEnter cancels close, and the pointer-intent latches hasPointerMoveOpenedRef / wasClickCloseRef / wasEscapeCloseRef that gate re-open. The port has NO pointer open at all (only click+keyboard). (2) NavigationMenuSub — a nested non-root provider (isRootMenu=false, no close-timer, no DismissableLayer root-dismiss, onTriggerEnter opens immediately). (3) Inline (non-viewport) Content mode: a per-Item Presence-mounted DismissableLayer Content with data-motion (to-start/to-end/from-start/from-end computed from collection index vs previousValue), pointerEvents:none while animating-closed on root, onPointerDownOutside / onFocusOutside dismissal rules. (4) The real content↔trigger tab-order proxy: removeFromTabOrder/restoreContentTabOrder (sets tabindex=-1 on content tabbables while closed, restores on entry) and the Tab/Shift+Tab key handler inside Content that walks tabbable candidates and falls through to the FocusProxy at the edges — the port stubs the FocusProxy span but wires no onFocus/onKeyDown logic. (5) Multi-content viewport registration: upstream registers EVERY item's Content into the viewport map and keeps the last-active one mounted (activeContentValue = previousValue while animating out); the port renders only the single currently-open content. (6) Link onSelect custom-event + ROOT_CONTENT_DISMISS dispatch (link click closes the root content). (7) disabled trigger handling (data-disabled, skip in pointer/roving).
_Coverage today:_ Four committed oracles + three APG checks cover a narrow happy path. DOM: navigationmenu.open.txt (defaultValue="one", viewport mode, 2 items, Item One open: trigger data-state=open/aria-expanded=true/aria-controls, FocusProxy visually-hidden span + aria-owns span, the indicator-track relative div, Indicator data-state=visible with translateX/width, Viewport data-state=open with --radix-navigation-menu-viewport-width/height vars, proxied Content with aria-labelledby + two links data-radix-collection-item) and navigationmenu.closed.txt (both triggers data-state=closed/aria-expanded=false, no content/viewport/indicator). aria: navigationmenu.open.txt/rest.txt + axe (open expects aria-hidden-focus, from the tabindex=0 aria-hidden FocusProxy). APG (themes-apg.mjs): ArrowRight/ArrowLeft rove between the two triggers NON-looping; ArrowDown on open trigger moves focus into content first link; Escape closes + returns focus to the trigger. themes-states driver `open` waits for measured indicator+viewport vars; `closed` waits for the rest trigger. NO closing oracle (sync unmount, deliberately dropped). So covered: the at-rest pixel/DOM contract, the single open-via-defaultValue DOM contract, basic horizontal LTR trigger roving, the entry-key + Escape keyboard, the aria-tree + axe. Everything below is uncovered.
- [core/missing-in-port/pointer] **Pointer-driven open via delayDuration (hover trigger → delayed open after 200ms)**
  - navigation-menu.tsx:106 delayDuration=200; :155-170 handleDelayedOpen; :188-192 onTriggerEnter; Trigger onPointerMove :510-523 → New themes-states driver `hoveropen`: pg.hover the first trigger, wait delayDuration, assert button[aria-expanded=true] + content mounted. Timer-racy → needs a special driver that hovers then waits/polls (not a stable DOM snapshot of the timer itself, but the post-open DOM is deterministic). Pair with a runtime check that a hover (not click) opened it.

  - navigation-menu.tsx:107 skipDelayDuration=300; :118-134 onChange sets isOpenDelayed via skipDelayTimerRef; :190-191 → Runtime check driver: open item A (hover), leave (close after 150ms), within 300ms hover item B → opens with NO 200ms delay. Assert timing delta. Timer-racy; runtime-only, not a DOM snapshot.

(2) CHECKBOX/RADIO ITEMS + ItemIndicator — role=menuitemcheckbox/menuitemradio, aria-checked (true/false/mixed), data-state checked/unchecked/indeterminate, the RadioGroup value context, the Presence-gated indicator span. (4) DISABLED-ITEM SKIP in roving — navigate() walks raw indices with no disabled filter, so a disabled item becomes a focusable tab stop (upstream RovingFocusGroup.Item focusable={!disabled} excludes it). (5) LONG-PRESS touch open (700ms timer, whenTouchOrPen) and the native-context-menu-when-disabled trigger path. (6) window `blur` → close. ### Popover — 21 gaps (0 core) · gaps-core
_Port-code needed:_ Genuinely missing PORT implementation (needs new code, not just an oracle): (1) MODAL mode — upstream Popover supports modal={true}: RemoveScroll scroll-lock, aria-hidden hideOthers on all siblings, trapFocus=true via FocusScope trapped, disableOutsidePointerEvents, and the right-click-outside focus-restore suppression. The Envelope (hideOthers/lockScroll/addFocusGuards) and ScrollLock primitives ALREADY EXIST (Dialog uses them) so this is wiring, but the port hardcodes non-modal (Input has no `modal` field; render never branches; only addFocusGuards/removeFocusGuards run). (2) PopoverAnchor sub-part (custom anchor decoupling position from trigger; hasCustomAnchor context flips whether trigger wraps in Popper.Anchor) — entirely absent. (3) PopoverClose sub-part (a button inside content that calls onOpenChange(false)) — absent; the port content is opaque PlainHTML with no Close wiring. (4) PopoverArrow sub-part (Popper arrow element) — absent. (5) forceMount (render content while closed for external animation libs) and container (portal target override) — absent. (6) The non-modal trigger re-open guard: upstream onInteractOutside checks targetIsTrigger and preventDefault so clicking the trigger doesn't close-then-immediately-reopen; the port's PointerDown closes on ANY outside-content pointerdown including on the trigger — a real behavioral bug (trigger click while open will run BOTH the dismiss-close and the TriggerClicked toggle). (7) onFocusOutside / focusin-after-pointerdown suppression (Safari container tabIndex case) — DismissableLayer port has no focusOutside path. (8) onOpenAutoFocus/onCloseAutoFocus customization hooks. (9) Multi-instance: the port doc admits "v1: single instance per page (fixed ids)" — though contentId is now useId-generated, the wrapper/portal adoption + focus-guard depth across stacked popovers is unproven.
_Coverage today:_ Three committed oracles + one runtime check cover the port, all in the single default config (non-modal, side=bottom, align=start per the themes golden; the gallery story is side=bottom align=center). (2) DOM closing oracle popover.closing.txt via themes-closing-dom.mjs + CLOSE.popover=Escape — verifies the lingering data-state=closed content node (Presence exit) with focus guards still up and aria-expanded=false on the trigger. (4) popover-portal.mjs runtime check (gallery ?story=popover): portal-to-body, data-side/align stamped + off-origin coords, focus-moves-into-content on open, Escape closes + restores focus to trigger, outside-click dismiss. (2) FORM PARTICIPATION — the hidden bubble <input type=radio aria-hidden tabindex=-1> per item (with name/value/required/disabled/form + the translateX(-100%)/opacity:0/absolute style), gated on a form-control/name Input flag, dispatching a bubbling change so native form onChange + checkValidity work; plus the consumer-stopPropagation suppression path. Lower-priority port limitations: Maybe-typed Input.value conflates uncontrolled with controlled-null (can't force a reset-to-nothing-checked, can't honor a parent that blocks the change); no per-item onKeyDown passthrough; no forceMount indicator; Home/End currently CHECK on move whereas upstream only moves focus (selection-follows-focus is arrow-key-only).
_Coverage today:_ DOM oracle: ONE state — radiogroup.checked.txt (golden-dom), captured by the themes-states.mjs `radiogroup.checked` driver (click value="2", assert data-state checked/unchecked). APG (themes-apg.mjs, id=radiogroup): 3 keyboard checks — (1) Tab lands on checked radio + exactly-one-tabbable roving tabindex; (2) ArrowDown moves+checks next, previous unchecks; (3) ArrowUp from first wraps to last+checks. Seed is only TWO items (Default/Comfortable), defaultValue="1", labelOutside, no item ids, no indicator span, no form. No closing oracle (non-overlay, correctly excluded). So covered: at-rest + single-selection + 2-item vertical roving with selection-follows-focus + entry-focus tabindex + Enter-no-activate is implied by ArrowDown driver but NOT explicitly tested.

### Accordion — 17 gaps (0 core) · gaps-core
_Port-code needed:_ Two genuine PORT-CODE bugs in HeadersKeyDown (Accordion.purs:338-350): (1) Navigation origin is wrong — it computes `current = tabStopIndex st` (first OPEN item, else 0) instead of the index of the ACTUALLY FOCUSED trigger. Upstream (accordion.tsx:235-240) derives triggerIndex from `event.target`. So pressing ArrowDown while focused on trigger #2 moves relative to the open item / index 0, not from #2 — roving is broken for any focus position other than the open/first item. Fix: resolve the focused trigger element (event.target / document.activeElement) to its item index and pass that as `current`. (2) Disabled triggers are NOT excluded from the navigable set. Upstream filters `getItems().filter(item => !item.ref.current?.disabled)` and indexes/counts within the ENABLED subset, so arrows skip disabled triggers. The port uses `count = length st.items` and `tabStopIndex` over ALL items, then guards `when (not disabled)` at the destination — landing on a disabled trigger becomes a no-op instead of skipping to the next enabled one. Fix: build the enabled-trigger index list and navigate within it. (3) Missing `aria-disabled` on the trigger: upstream (accordion.tsx:452) stamps `aria-disabled={(open && !collapsible) || undefined}` so the single non-collapsible open trigger announces as disabled; the port (Accordion.purs:240-256) never emits aria-disabled. (4) Upstream keyboard nav ALWAYS loops (moveNext/movePrev hardcode wrap, accordion.tsx:249-261) regardless of any loop prop; the port exposes a `loop` flag — with loop=false it diverges from upstream (default true happens to match).
_Coverage today:_ Golden DOM (accordion.open.txt) covers the static open/closed structure: data-state, data-orientation, aria-expanded, aria-controls(open-only), id↔aria-labelledby linkage, role=region, the content var-alias style, and the closed `hidden` panel + data-radix-collection-item. golden-aria rest/open snapshot the accessibility tree (heading level=3, button [expanded], region name) with empty axe violations. themes-states.mjs has ONE accordion driver (`open`: click first trigger → wait region open) feeding themes-a11y/open-dom. There are ZERO accordion entries in themes-apg.mjs — no keyboard/roving/Home/End/orientation/RTL/loop/disabled-skip coverage at all. No multiple-type, single-collapsible, controlled, or disabled-item golden variants exist.

  - accordion.tsx:235-240,300-301 (triggerIndex = findIndex(item.ref.current === target); focus triggerCollection[clampedIndex]) → themes-apg.mjs accordion check: focus trigger #2, press ArrowDown, assert document.activeElement is trigger #3 (not #1). Currently the port would compute from tabStopIndex and move wrong.
- [core/partial/keyboard] **Disabled triggers are excluded from the navigable collection; arrows skip OVER them to the next enabled trigger**
  - accordion.tsx:236 (getItems().filter(item => !item.ref.current?.disabled)); count/index within filtered set → themes-apg.mjs: render 3 items with #2 disabled; focus #1, ArrowDown, assert focus lands on #3 (enabled), not #2. Port currently lands on disabled #2 → no-op.

### AccessibleIcon — 8 gaps (0 core) · gaps-core
_Port-code needed:_ Yes — the canonical port (Hydrogen.Radix.AccessibleIcon) needs a structural rewrite to faithfully reproduce upstream: (1) emit a Fragment (no outer wrapper span) — Halogen has no Fragment node, so adopt the Themes.AccessibleIcon approach of returning `Array (HH.HTML w i)` (icon sibling + label sibling) and splice into the parent; (2) inject aria-hidden=\"true\" AND focusable=\"false\" ONTO the icon element itself rather than wrapping it in an inner aria-hidden span — since Halogen children are opaque HH.HTML and cannot be cloned/attr-injected the way React.cloneElement does, this requires either (a) the API take the icon as a builder that the primitive can decorate (e.g. accept the svg's attribute array, or a `IProp` injector), or (b) keep requiring callers to pre-author aria-hidden/focusable but document/enforce it. (a) is the only way to truly match the contract without caller cooperation. (3) enforce single-child via the type (single `HH.HTML`, not `Array`). No pointer/timer/multi-thumb/layer behavior is involved — this is a static a11y-attribute injection primitive.
_Coverage today:_ At-rest PIXEL only. `accessibleicon` is listed in testing/playwright/themes-capture.sh (committed golden testing/golden/themes/golden/accessibleicon.png) and rendered by testing/golden/themes/src/app.tsx (id "accessibleicon", a Flex with a 15x15 gear svg + label "Settings"). The port side renders the same gear in examples/themes-port/src/ThemesPort/Main.purs accessibleiconPage. Critically: `accessibleicon` is NOT a key in testing/playwright/scripts/themes-states.mjs STATES, so it is excluded from every behavioral oracle — themes-a11y.mjs MATRIX = Object.keys(STATES) → no axe / no ARIA-tree snapshot; themes-open-dom.mjs / themes-dom.mjs (interactive ?c=&s=) has no accessibleicon entry; themes-apg.mjs has none; no closing oracle (no presence/exit). So the ONLY thing verified is the visible pixels (which by design are JUST the icon, since the label is visually-hidden). The component's entire functional contract — aria-hidden="true" and focusable="false" on the icon, and the visually-hidden label being present in the a11y tree — is INVISIBLE to a pixel diff and is currently UNVERIFIED.

_Port-code needed:_ The port is MISSING substantial Root-level behavior that needs new implementation, not just oracles: (1) PASTE handling — upstream intercepts onPaste on the Root div, sanitizes the clipboard text, slices to collection.size, sets the whole value, and focuses the last filled slot (lines 478-485, dispatch PASTE 360-372). (2) Multi-char onInput / autocomplete-paste — when a password manager dumps the full code into one input (value.length>1), upstream treats it as a paste (lines 689-703). The port's onValueInput only takes lastChar, silently dropping the rest. (3) Enter → attemptSubmit/form.requestSubmit (lines 813-816) and autoSubmit when all slots filled (lines 431-442) + onAutoSubmit callback + form reset listener (lines 419-426). Port has no form wiring, no hidden-input ref submit, no Enter handler. (4) Delete/Clear/Cut semantics — upstream distinguishes Backspace (clear+retreat), Delete (clear-in-place, no retreat), Clear/Ctrl+Backspace (clear ALL), Cut (clear+stay) via userActionRef state machine (lines 327-358, 671-737, 771-812). Port only handles Backspace. (5) onPointerDown that preventDefaults and clamps focus to min(index,lastSelectableIndex) so you can't click an unreachable slot (lines 886-891). (6) onFocus → currentTarget.select() (line 670) so re-typing replaces. (7) Replace-when-full + select-on-last (SET_CHAR lines 303-324) and the mid-selection char-insertion path (keydown lines 836-882). (8) disabled/readOnly/type=password/placeholder/autoComplete/autoFocus props and the per-slot Input as a real sub-component taking index/onInvalidChange. (9) onInvalidChange callback + requestAnimationFrame re-select on invalid (lines 761-769). (10) re-validation when validationType changes (lines 379-389). (11) isFocusable gating (only slots up to lastSelectableIndex are focusable; the port makes every slot a roving target regardless of fill, lines 632-645).
_Coverage today:_ Three DOM oracles (otp.{filled,empty,typed}) + two a11y oracles (otp.{rest,filled} aria-snapshot, both with empty axe = no violations) + three APG checks (themes-apg.mjs:471/485/494: ArrowRight/Left rove + tab-stop migration; End/Home; type-char auto-advance). themes-states.mjs otp drivers: filled (at-rest defaultValue=123, hidden=123), empty (all slots empty, hidden empty), typed (focus slot0 + type "45" → slots 4/5, slot2 tabindex=0). ### Avatar — 17 gaps (0 core) · gaps-core
_Port-code needed:_ PORT-CODE genuinely missing/divergent (not just unverified):

1. LOAD STRATEGY DIVERGENCE (root cause of most gaps). Upstream useImageLoadingStatus (avatar.tsx:141-184) probes loading with a DETACHED `new window.Image()`, listening for load/error on that probe, and only mounts the real `<Primitive.img>` once status==='loaded' (avatar.tsx:99-101). The port instead ALWAYS mounts a visible `<img>` (when src/="") and reads load status from that visible element's HE.onLoad/HE.onError (Avatar.purs:141-153). Consequences the port cannot reproduce: (a) the real <img> is never in the DOM during loading/idle/error — port leaks a half-loaded/broken <img> into the tree during loading and on error; upstream guarantees `queryByRole('img')` is absent unless loaded (test lines 71-74, 324-327, 351-361). (b) On error the port keeps the broken <img> mounted alongside the fallback; upstream removes it.

2. naturalWidth===0 => 'error' semantics MISSING. getImageLoadingStatus (avatar.tsx:186-188) maps a fired `load` with naturalWidth===0 to 'error', not 'loaded'. Port's HE.onLoad unconditionally sets Loaded (Avatar.purs:152). Tests at lines 155-185 assert fallback shown and onLoadingStatusChange('error') in this case. Port cannot detect naturalWidth without the detached-probe approach.

3. delayMs MISSING entirely (acknowledged in port header comment lines 19-22). Upstream AvatarFallback (avatar.tsx:122-129) gates fallback render behind a setTimeout(delayMs); fallback is absent until the delay elapses (tests 251-275). Port shows fallback immediately whenever status/=Loaded. No Input field for delayMs.

4. onLoadingStatusChange / Output('idle') contract PARTIAL. Upstream fires the callback on every status change EXCEPT it never surfaces 'idle' while mounted (test 215-219: "is not called with 'idle'"), and fires 'error' when src is missing (test 210-213). Port's StatusChanged Output can emit Idle (Receive sets Idle when src=="" — Avatar.purs:174, raised at 183), and for empty src the port emits Idle, NOT Errored — upstream treats missing/empty src as 'error' (avatar.tsx:156-158). This is a behavioral mismatch in the Output stream.

5. empty-src / missing-src => 'error' MISSING. Upstream: no src or src="" sets status 'error' (avatar.tsx:156-158), so onLoadingStatusChange('error') fires and fallback shows. Port maps src=="" to Idle (Avatar.purs:130,174). Observable difference in both Output and any error-targeted styling.

6. crossOrigin / referrerPolicy pass-through MISSING. Upstream forwards referrerPolicy & crossOrigin to the probe Image (avatar.tsx:169-172) AND spreads imageProps (incl. these) onto the mounted img. Port's Input has no crossOrigin/referrerPolicy; renderImage (Avatar.purs:147-154) emits only src/alt/class/data-state. referrerPolicy materially changes whether the image loads (tests 278-362).

7. Arbitrary prop spread MISSING. Upstream Avatar/Image/Fallback are Primitive.* spreading all props (asChild, id, role, style, data-*, event handlers). Port exposes a fixed Input (src/alt/fallback/style) with no escape hatch — no asChild, no arbitrary attrs/handlers on root/image/fallback.

8. Multiple-image dev warning: intentionally out of scope (dev-only console.warn, avatar.tsx:195-223) — acceptable to skip, but note the port also does not structurally prevent/observe multiple images (single-img model only).

9. data-state placement: upstream avatar.tsx does NOT emit data-state at all on the primitive (radix-ui PRIMITIVE avatar has no data-state; data-state on avatar is a @radix-ui/THEMES concern). Port emits data-state on the <img> (Avatar.purs:151). Verify this matches the THEMES golden source, not the primitive — possible spurious attribute vs the primitive contract.
_Coverage today:_ Only at-rest pixel oracles: testing/golden/themes/golden/avatar.png and storybook __visual__/themes-avatar--{solid,soft}.png (these target Hydrogen.Themes.Avatar, the styled preset). These are STATELESS single-frame snapshots of the rendered tree (fallback present and/or a loaded <img>). No interactive oracle id exists in the themes-states / themes-open-dom / themes-a11y / themes-apg harnesses for Avatar. None of the load-lifecycle transitions, delayMs, error path, src-change reset, onLoadingStatusChange contract, alt/a11y, referrerPolicy/crossOrigin, or naturalWidth=0 semantics are verified anywhere. The buck2 _check typecheck confirms it compiles; it does not verify any runtime behavior.

### VisuallyHidden — 7 gaps (0 core) · gaps-core
_Port-code needed:_ The port is structurally narrower than upstream and needs three real additions to be faithful: (1) asChild/Slot support so the clip style + props project onto a caller element instead of always emitting a wrapping <span> — this is the canonical VisuallyHidden usage and is the single biggest gap; (2) arbitrary prop pass-through (id, aria-*, data-*, title, dir, event handlers) — currently the API surface is only `ClassNames + children`, which blocks aria-labelledby/id wiring; (3) user style merge (caller style overriding/extending VISUALLY_HIDDEN_STYLES), e.g. the focus-to-unhide skip-link pattern. ref forwarding is the fourth but is idiom-dependent in Halogen and may be declared N/A. None of these require state — they widen the render function's prop surface and add an asChild variant.
_Coverage today:_ No interactive oracle. The primitive is stateless/presentational: a single `<span>` carrying a fixed clip style. There is no dedicated VisuallyHidden oracle id; its only verification is incidental — wherever a composed component (e.g. Dialog title/description, ScrollArea, etc.) embeds visually-hidden content, the at-rest DOM/pixel snapshots cover it indirectly. There is no direct golden/*.png at-rest pixel test nor a stateless DOM snapshot pinned to this module. The `inlineStyle` string is asserted only by reading the source, not by any oracle. Net: effectively unverified in isolation.

_Port-code needed:_ The port (Hydrogen/Radix/Label.purs) is missing the ONLY non-trivial behavior react-label adds over a bare <label>: the onMouseDown handler (label.tsx:19-27) that (a) returns early when the mousedown target is inside a button/input/select/textarea, and (b) otherwise calls preventDefault when event.detail > 1 and the event is not already defaultPrevented, to suppress text selection on double/multi-click. To reproduce this in Halogen the label render fn must attach an onMouseDown handler (via Halogen.HTML.Events) that runs equivalent logic: inspect event.detail and event.target.closest('button, input, select, textarea'), and conditionally preventDefault. This requires raising `label` from a pure PlainHTML render fn to one that can emit an action/handler (HH.HTML with an event), or providing an FFI mousedown handler. Secondarily, the port should accept native prop/attribute passthrough (id, data-*, aria-*, title, style, arbitrary handlers) instead of the fixed {for, class_} record, to match PrimitiveLabelProps spread (label.tsx:11-12,17). asChild/Slot and ref-forwarding are architectural divergences that are reasonable to omit by design.
_Coverage today:_ Coverage is at-rest pixel only. A single golden PNG (testing/playwright/golden/label.png) captured from the static story components-label--styled (examples/src/Gallery/Story/Label.purs), which renders one label with for:"" inside a display:contents wrapper. The story is stateless (Gallery.staticStory). There is NO interactive oracle (no themes-states/apg/a11y/open-dom id for Label), no keyboard/pointer driver, and no runtime/unit assertion on Label behavior. capture-goldens.mjs:27 registers id "label" → story "components-label--styled" — pixel snapshot of resting appearance only. The port (Hydrogen/Radix/Label.purs) is a pure stateless render fn: `label { for, class_ }` and `label_`, emitting `HH.label [HP.for, classes]`. It carries NO event handlers and exposes NO prop passthrough beyond for+class.

(2) CheckboxItem and RadioGroup/RadioItem variants (+ ItemIndicator presence) — new MenuEntry constructors with role=menuitemcheckbox/menuitemradio, aria-checked, data-state, controlled selection. (3) Disabled TRIGGERS (Menu.disabled field → non-focusable, roving-skip, cross-menu-candidate filter) and disabled-ITEM skip in vertical roving/typeahead. (4) Typeahead search buffer inside content (and disabled-item skip in it). (5) RTL-aware cross-menu arrows and loop=false cross-menu (thread st.dir/st.loop into adjacentMenu). (6) pointerDown left-button/ctrlKey discrimination + focus-competition preventDefault, and the hasInteractedOutsideRef nuance (don't refocus trigger on outside-click close). (7) MenubarArrow, MenubarGroup, MenubarLabel sub-parts; forceMount.
_Coverage today:_ DOM oracles: menubar.open (File menu open: trigger bar with 3 role=menuitem buttons, data-state/aria-expanded/aria-controls/aria-haspopup, popper wrapper, role=menu content with 4 entries incl. a separator, focus-guard sentinels, content custom-property vars) and menubar.item1 (ArrowDown highlights first item → data-highlighted + roving tabindex=0). ARIA snapshots: menubar.rest (3 menuitems, no menu) and menubar.open (File [expanded] + nested menu tree); both have axe passes (menubar.rest.axe / menubar.open.axe). APG keyboard (themes-apg.mjs): ArrowRight/ArrowLeft rove triggers (loop), Home/End first/last trigger, ArrowDown-on-closed-trigger opens+focuses first item, inside-menu ArrowDown/Up rove (loop), ArrowRight-inside-menu opens adjacent menu, Escape closes+restores trigger focus. NO closing oracle (bare primitive content has animation-name:none → unmounts synchronously; deliberately dropped). All drivers keyed off upstream role/data-* so they run against golden AND port. Covered behaviors: open/closed at-rest, single-menu-open invariant, horizontal roving on the bar, vertical roving in content, ArrowDown/Up open, cross-menu Arrow, Escape close+restore, first-item highlight, aria-controls only-while-open.
- [core/partial/keyboard] **Enter/Space on a CLOSED trigger toggles the menu open (keyboard). Upstream onKeyDown: if key is Enter or ' ' → onMenuToggle; also preventDefault + sets wasKeyboardTriggerOpenRef so the content auto-focuses first item via onEntryFocus. ### Dialog — 20 gaps (0 core) · gaps-core
_Port-code needed:_ Genuinely missing PORT-CODE behavior (not just unverified): (1) DialogClose wiring — content passed as opaque PlainHTML means there is NO close-button path; the golden's Cancel button is inert. This is the most important core gap. (2) Non-modal mode — modal=false still renders the overlay, traps Tab, and locks scroll; upstream renders no overlay, no trap, no lock, no hideOthers, with interact-outside-tracked focus restore. Effectively unimplemented. (3) Right-click / ctrl-click outside guard — port closes on any left overlay click but lacks the pointerdown-outside right-click veto. (4) Trigger-as-outside-target guard (targetIsTrigger) — risk of close-then-reopen when the trigger is clicked while open. (5) Consumer-preventable callbacks (onOpenAutoFocus/onCloseAutoFocus/onPointerDownOutside/onInteractOutside/onFocusOutside/onEscapeKeyDown) — none exposed. (6) forceMount and Portal container props. (7) Nested/overlapping modal layer stack — body pointer-events restore is unconditional, so an inner dialog closing unlocks the body while an outer dialog is still open. (8) Title tag is <h1> vs upstream <h2>, and empty title/description arrays still emit stray empty <h1>/<p> nodes (upstream renders nothing). (9) aria-labelledby/aria-describedby are conditional in the port but unconditional upstream.
_Coverage today:_ Oracles today cover a narrow happy path. DOM goldens: dialog.open.txt (open modal — body[data-scroll-locked], focus-guard sentinels, hideOthers aria-hidden on #root, themed overlay>scroll>scrollPadding>content tree, trigger aria-expanded/haspopup/controls/data-state=open, content role=dialog + aria-labelledby/describedby + tabindex=-1 + data-state=open, h1 title + p description) and dialog.closing.txt (lingering data-state=closed node through pinned exit anim; body pointer-events released but data-scroll-locked still set). ARIA goldens: dialog.open.txt accessibility tree + dialog.rest.txt (button only) + empty axe (no violations) for open & rest. APG (themes-apg.mjs): 3 runtime checks — focus moves into dialog on open, Tab trapped (6 presses stay within), Escape closes + returns focus to #root button. States harness drives open via trigger click; CLOSE.dialog drives Escape exit. NOTHING covers: DialogClose, non-modal mode, forceMount, portal container, right-click outside guard, the *AutoFocus/*Outside callback prevention semantics, controlled-prop sync, aria-controls absence while closed (only implicitly in closing golden), h2-vs-h1 title tag, always-present aria-describedby, missing-title/description dev warnings, focus loop wrap direction, trigger re-click on outside.

### Tooltip — 22 gaps (0 core) · gaps-core
_Port-code needed:_ PORT-CODE genuinely missing (not just unverified):
1. aria-describedby should be conditional on open (tooltip.tsx:290). Port emits it always (Tooltip.purs:215) — closed trigger wrongly references a hidden id. CORE a11y bug.
2. data-state tri-state. Port hardcodes 'delayed-open' for every open path (Tooltip.purs:216,237). Focus-open must be 'instant-open'; pointer-open is 'delayed-open' only after a real delay. Currently semantically wrong on focus.
3. Open/close delay machinery (delayDuration/skipDelayDuration, Provider). Port opens synchronously — the module header acknowledges delayMs is a follow-up. This is the single biggest behavioral divergence: a 'tooltip' that appears instantly on hover is a different UX contract.
4. pointerdown/click closes the tooltip and pointerdown suppresses the focus-open flash (tooltip.tsx:308-319). Entirely absent — clicking the trigger leaves the tooltip stuck open.
5. Touch guard: port uses onMouseEnter/Leave; upstream onPointerMove ignores pointerType==='touch'. Touch devices should not hover-open.
6. Hoverable content + grace polygon (tooltip.tsx:408-481) and the disableHoverableContent prop. Port unmounts on trigger mouseleave, so a user can never move the pointer into the tooltip content. Edge but a real feature loss.
7. Close-on-other-tooltip-open (TOOLTIP_OPEN CustomEvent, tooltip.tsx:182,524-527). No cross-instance coordination — multiple tooltips can be open at once.
8. Close-on-trigger-scroll (tooltip.tsx:530-540). Port repositions on scroll instead of closing.
9. aria-label override for the VisuallyHidden role=tooltip accessible name (tooltip.tsx:570-572). No way to give the tooltip an accessible name distinct from its visible content.
10. onPointerDownOutside dismissal and the preventable onEscapeKeyDown/onPointerDownOutside callbacks. Port is Escape-only by design (documented in header) — pointer-outside dismiss is a deliberate divergence to either implement or formally document; the preventable-escape hook is simply missing.
11. asChild trigger (Popper.Anchor asChild + composeEventHandlers): port owns a fixed button and cannot compose consumer trigger props/handlers.
12. forceMount/container Portal props, and Presence-driven mount/unmount: port keeps a mounted-but-display:none content when closed where upstream UNMOUNTS (so closed-state DOM differs).
_Coverage today:_ Two non-circular oracle families touch tooltip. (1) DOM golden: golden-dom/tooltip.open.txt pins the open shape — trigger button with aria-describedby=<id0>, data-state=delayed-open, data-radix-popper-side/align; the position:fixed wrapper; rt-TooltipContent with data-side/align/state; visible label <p>; arrow span+svg; and the VisuallyHidden span id=<id0> role=tooltip carrying the duplicated label. Driver = STATES.tooltip.open (hover trigger, wait for role=tooltip). (2) ARIA golden: golden-aria/tooltip.open.txt (accessibility tree: button, paragraph, img, tooltip+nested paragraph) and tooltip.rest.txt (button only); plus axe scans (open/rest). (3) APG: two checks — focus shows the tooltip; Escape hides the tooltip. (4) Closing-DOM and themes-states richer-state matrix DELIBERATELY exclude tooltip (commented: Content unmounts on hide, no lingering data-state=closed node). So today's verified contract is: open DOM/ARIA snapshot, focus-opens, Escape-closes. Everything timing-, pointer-, controlled-, and multi-instance-related is unverified.
